body:
> Our thinking is that by not having a connects_to on the model, the model is using the connection that’s used on ActiveRecord::Base. But the migration checker also uses the connection on ActiveRecord::Base to do the migration

Yea, `BaseRecord` inherits from the parent class, in this case `ApplicationRecord` which is set up to be the same connection as `ActiveRecord::Base`, but this would have been true in the past as well. Pending migrations check wasn't working for multiple databases until the 7.1 release so I think we would have seen this in 7.0 if it hadn't been broken. If a class doesn't set its own explicit connection, it will use whatever the next connection is in the inheritance chain, which by default will always fall back to `ActiveRecord::Base`.

> And a thought was to fix it with with_temporary_connection_for_each so that it is ok for there to be an existing pool that can be set aside when running the migration-related queries.

I'm confused - `check_pending_migrations` is [already using](https://github.com/rails/rails/blob/main/activerecord/lib/active_record/migration.rb#L771-L774) `with_temporary_connection_for_each`. Do you mean to use that somewhere else?

As a note, I found that this also doesn't reproduce when eager loading the application.

~Also to narrow this down, the issue here isn't related to multiple databases, I can reproduce it without `AnimalsRecord` by just calling `establish_connection` in `ApplicationRecord`.~

Edit: ok actually it's not related to `AnimalsRecord` but it is related to having multiple configs in the config file. I thought this was maybe related to a different issue I had fixed with migrations but it's actually a little different.

Thank you for looking into this 💖 

>> And a thought was to fix it with with_temporary_connection_for_each so that it is ok for there to be an existing pool that can be set aside when running the migration-related queries.
> 
> I'm confused - check_pending_migrations is [already using](https://github.com/rails/rails/blob/main/activerecord/lib/active_record/migration.rb#L771-L774) with_temporary_connection_for_each. Do you mean to use that somewhere else?

Oops, sorry, I think the notes I took from talking with @matthewd aren't great 🥵 I think the idea was: if there is already an existing database connection pool, put it aside, and then create a new database connection-pool specifically to do the migration-related queries, and then put back the original connection pool afterwards.

> if there is already an existing database connection pool, put it aside, and then create a new database connection-pool specifically to do the migration-related queries, and then put back the original connection pool afterwards.

So creating a special class to run migration related queries (or anything in the rake tasks) was my original intention when adding `with_temporary_connection_for_each` but it's hard AF to actually get that working in the active record tests and I honestly got a little burnt out on trying to make it work. Far too much of the test framework expects `ActiveRecord::Base.connection` to Just Work.

My ultimate goal is to never clobber connections. I just don't know a straightforward way to get there.

Chatted with Matthew and we came up with a way to bandaid fix this particular issue (we can make a temporary class to establish connections on only for the pending migrations check). Then in 7.2/8.0 I'll fix it a better way that can't be backported. Fix incoming.

issue.title: Use custom class for pending migrations connection
issue.body:
In bensheldon/good_job#1103 it was reported that a connection not established is being seen when there are multiple configs for an environment (a multi-db app).

While I think that something is happening where Good Job is accessing the connection while we're checking for pending migrations, this could happen in other gems if we're clobbering the connection on `ActiveRecord::Base` that is needed.

Here we are making a special class to establish connections to the database. Because the class does not inherit from `Base` and establishes it's own connection, it won't clobber any existing connections on `Base`, leaving them in-tact while the app boots.

The reason this wasn't seen in 7.0 is because pending migrations didn't check all the available configs. Once that was fixed this error appeared.

I didn't add a test for this because it's really hard to reproduce without good job and actually booting a server and running a request.

Fixes: #49689

body:
I'm seeing something similar in our app, which mostly doesn't use `connects_to`, when the code is reloaded and Active Record clears all reloadable connections:
https://github.com/rails/rails/blob/26f8edf411bee476049507cab2e59e4dffafca30/activerecord/lib/active_record/railtie.rb#L301-L310

However, we're not seeing a deadlock but each role/pool in sequence times out "attempting to checkout all existing connections".

Removing the pending migrations check with `config.active_record.migration_error = nil` solves the issue, but I can't see anything in /rails/locks with the DebugLocks middleware.

I started looking at removing `ActiveRecord::PendingMigrationConnection` because it seemed off but that led me here.

@eileencodes Can you share the better way to fix the issue that couldn't be backported that doesn't involve having that class?

> I'm seeing something similar in our app, which mostly doesn't use connects_to, when the code is reloaded and Active Record clears all reloadable connections:

Why is this showing up now though and wasn't before? When did this start happening in our app? I'm not sure it's this change, this has been in Rails since October 🤔 

> @eileencodes Can you share the better way to fix the issue that couldn't be backported that doesn't involve having that class?

I actually don't recall what I was thinking exactly. I think there's this broader fix of having a yaml that defines connections so we can establish connections on the actual class for the connection rather than reuse AR::Base or this new class and clobbering connections. But even if we implemented that in Rails finally, it won't work for Shopify until Podding is gone.

It's not particularly recent, and I don't think it's related to the PR that fixed this issue.
It's just that the issue is very similar where some connection is owned by a thread and `attempt_to_checkout_all_existing_connections` wants to check it out and times out (here it deadlocked apparently).

With the recent connection lease changes, all the other connections seem to be leased in `DatabaseTasks`, but for this one we use `establish_connection` and `remove_connection_pool`, so I was wondering if this wasn't the one causing my troubles.

I found the issue, we had a call to `ActiveRecord::Base.connection` during the boot process. This results in a lock timeout when code reloading happens.
I can repro this in 7.1.0 and 7.0 as well: https://github.com/etiennebarrie/rails-app/tree/49689

It seems like the code is trying to handle connections for `ActiveSupport::IsolatedExecutionState.context`: https://github.com/etiennebarrie/rails-app/tree/49689

which I would expect to handle the `ActiveRecord::Base.connection` but it seems like it doesn't.
